_note: Day 5 shift: a computer sends data out. Built by the generic path of LogGenerator (event "transfer"). The first rule is a "lookup" (the computer decides where it may send), the second a "threshold" (transfers an hour), the third an "info" rule: SIZE is shown on the card and is never a rule, which is the lesson of the day (the 9,000 MB backup is fine, the 2 MB trickle is the leak). The threat is the unapproved host 198.51.100.23 that repeats in bad logs.

comments.short: Joshua: No mistakes, but too few logs. Be quicker.

hud_line: Approved places per computer    On call tonight: {on_call}

rules.name: Where
rules.text: Each computer may send only to its own approved places.
details: web-01: the update server, the analytics partner.
rules.example_ok: backup-01 sends to the backup cloud
rules.why: Data should only go where somebody agreed it may go.
rules.broken: goes to a place that is not approved for that computer

rules.name: How often
rules.text: A computer makes at most 6 transfers an hour.
details: A steady trickle is a pattern. A person does not send data 12 times an hour.
rules.why: Programs send data on a timer. A short list of regular transfers is normal, a long one is worth a look.
rules.broken: is one of far too many in an hour

rules.name: Size
rules.text: Size is not a rule. It does not make a transfer good or bad.
details: A huge backup can be fine, and a tiny trickle can be a leak.
rules.example_ok: 9,000 MB, backup-01 to the backup cloud
rules.why: Look at where it goes and how often. The size alone decides nothing.

decoys.reason: 9,000 MB is huge, but it is the nightly backup, and backup-01 may send to the backup cloud.
The analytics partner is approved for web-01, and one small upload an hour is its schedule.
600 MB is a lot, but the update server is approved for web-01, and 2 an hour is few.
